title: Semantic turn detection sharply reduces interruptions in one voice-agent test
friendlyTitle: A voice agent interrupted callers much less often
summary: Veris added the Jev text classifier to one Pipecat voice agent and reran 100 simulated tasks three times. The share of caller turns interrupted fell from 52% to 11%, but task completion barely changed and median response time rose from 2.1 to 4.6 seconds.
friendlySummary: A test used meaning, not only silence, to decide when a caller had finished. Interruptions dropped a lot, but replies became slower and the agent did not complete more tasks.
whyItMatters: Knowing when a person has finished speaking can improve the feel of a voice assistant even when its underlying answers do not improve. The result also shows the trade-off: teams should test interruption, accuracy and delay together on their own callers and noise conditions.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Phone assistants can feel more polite when they wait properly. Businesses should also measure whether the extra waiting frustrates people or affects successful calls.
